subject: phlebotomy
intro: Phlebotomy leads into the front line of the clinical laboratory — the professionals whose venipuncture skill supplies every blood test, and the laboratory staff who process and run those specimens.

roles.title: Phlebotomists
roles.what: Draw blood for tests, transfusions, donations or research, explain the procedure to patients, and assist in the recovery of patients with adverse reactions to the draw.
roles.where: This is the course's central units put to work — circulatory anatomy and vein selection, the venipuncture procedure with its order of draw and tube additives, and the consent and patient-identification rules from the legal unit.

roles.title: Medical and Clinical Laboratory Technologists
roles.what: Perform complex medical laboratory tests for the diagnosis, treatment and prevention of disease, often training or supervising the technicians and phlebotomy staff who feed specimens into the lab.
roles.where: Specimen handling and processing, rejection criteria, and point-of-care testing from the course are the input side of the technologist's work, while blood composition knowledge underpins the haematology tests they run.

roles.title: Medical and Clinical Laboratory Technicians
roles.what: Perform routine medical laboratory tests for the diagnosis, treatment and prevention of disease, usually working under the supervision of a medical laboratory technologist.
roles.where: The processing and centrifugation and labelling-and-transport topics decide whether a technician's results mean anything — the same rejection criteria and handling discipline the course drills.

roles.title: Medical Assistants
roles.what: Perform administrative and clinical duties under a physician's direction: taking vital signs and medical histories, preparing patients for examination, drawing blood, and scheduling and record-keeping.
roles.where: Venipuncture technique, capillary collection and point-of-care testing give medical assistants their clinical drawing duties, and the course's patient-identification and confidentiality topics cover their records work.
